name: FRAMES
intro: FRAMES（Factuality, Retrieval, And reasoning MEasurement Set）是一个高质量数据集，旨在测试大型语言模型（LLMs）在生成最终答案时的事实性、检索能力和推理能力。该基准测试提供了一个统一的框架，用于评估LLMs在端到端检索增强生成（RAG）场景中的性能。FRAMES包含具有挑战性的多跳问题，需要整合来自多个来源的信息。
org: Harvard University, Google DeepMind, New York University, Duke University, University of Massachuset
intro_en: FRAMES (Factuality, Retrieval, And reasoning MEasurement Set) is a high-quality dataset designed to test large language models (LLMs) on factuality, retrieval ability, and reasoning when generating final answers. This benchmark provides a unified framework to evaluate LLMs' performance in end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios. FRAMES includes challenging multi-hop questions that require integrating information from multiple sources.

drawio_review_note:
Aligned with arXiv:2409.12941. FRAMES is a dataset of 824 test samples for evaluating factuality, retrieval, and reasoning in RAG systems. The paper first explored synthetic question generation from multiple Wikipedia articles but found substantial hallucinated questions and answers, so it relied on human annotation for the final evaluation set. Human annotators wrote questions, correct responses, and required Wikipedia article lists, then labeled each question by reasoning type such as numerical reasoning, tabular reasoning, multiple constraints, temporal reasoning, and post-processing. Additional quality checks re-annotated questions, verified correctness and groundedness to Wikipedia, removed hallucinations, and added temporal context when answers could drift. Evaluation then tests whether a RAG system retrieves relevant facts, reasons across articles, and synthesizes the correct final answer.

Bilingual Draw.io bundle synchronized from benchmark_importer after paper and official-source review. The Chinese and English specs use identical node IDs, semantic types, coordinates, edges, and waypoints; strict Draw.io validation, XML and link checks, and rendered-image visual review passed before publication.
